subject: Session-cache sizing & target unit economics for Integron pilot
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Clark <sara.clark@integronhealth.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@integronhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — session cache sizing & rough $/1M targets

Hi Sara / Tom — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can get a realistic costing model together: 

Key inputs we captured on the call:
- Expected pilot scope: ~12k unique end-user sessions/day, roughly 2.5M tokens/session on peak flows (some sessions are short, median ~120 tokens).
- Session pattern: ~70% of sessions start with a 1–2 message prompt series that is highly repetitive across users (templates + guidance text).
- SLA needs: p95 latency target ~450ms for interactive flows; availability: standard hosted SLA.

Caching assumptions to validate (what we used for the first-pass economics):
- Session-prefix caching (warm prefixes / reusable instruction text) coverage: we modeled a 35% prefix cache hit rate across tokens — this assumes we can capture the common opening blocks and sticky templates.
- Cold tokens (misses) still incur full inference cost; hit tokens are served from cached KV/prefetch and reduce effective per-token GPU work by ~75% in our model.

First-pass unit economics (ballpark, to align expectations):
- Nominal list price used: $120 / 1M tokens (model variant X quantized path).
- With 35% cache hit & batching/quantization recommendations applied, effective cost range we modeled: $48–$70 / 1M effective tokens (depends on sequence length distribution and batching).

Asks / next steps: 
1) Can you share a 24–72 hour sample of anonymized session telemetry (timestamps, session id, prompt token counts, whether templates were used)? I attached a tiny CSV template to make this easier. [Attachment: session_telemetry_template.csv]
2) If the pilot budget has a target effective price, please flag it — you mentioned a rough target in the call; I want to make sure our modeling converges on your acceptable band.
3) We'll run three hit-rate scenarios (25% / 40% / 60%) and return a spreadsheet showing per-1M token effective costs plus sensitivity to batching and quantization.

I'll also include a short mutual action plan draft for timelines and approvals. 

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

[Attachment: Integron_MA_plan_draft.pdf]
From: Sara Clark <sara.clark@integronhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@integronhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 19:43:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — session cache sizing & rough $/1M targets

Thanks Aditya — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we send telemetry: 

1) Pilot scale: the initial pilot will be constrained to 3k sessions/day (out of the 12k eventual target) for a 4-week run. Can you show numbers pro-rated for 3k/day as well?
2) Cache hit expectations: our internal engineering lead flagged that the shared templates only cover roughly 20–30% of tokens today (they're working to formalize templates but aren't there yet). Can you run the 25% / 40% / 60% scenarios you mentioned — 25% is the conservative baseline we expect if we don't change prompt design.
3) Budget context: for the pilot, procurement has allocated $18k–$40k for production inference costs over the month (not including Redwood platform/enterprise fees). Converted to effective token terms, our target for the pilot is closer to $45 / 1M effective tokens. If your model shows we're above that at realistic hit rates, we may need to look at a constrained feature set or different model sizing.

I'll attach a small export tonight and aim to send by EOD tomorrow. Also please include the assumptions around quantization and batching in the spreadsheet so our infra team can vet operational feasibility.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Clark
Head of Product | Integron Health
sara.clark@integronhealth.com | +1 415-555-0707
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap — session cache sizing & rough $/1M targets (internal)

Team — quick internal ask before I send the costing sheet back to Integron: 

Summary: client is likely to start pilot at 3k sessions/day; they expect conservative cache hit ~25% and target $45 / 1M effective tokens for pilot. Need our recommended configuration to hit ~ $45 / 1M at 25% and at 40% hit. Please focus on: 
- Model variant (float16 vs int8/4): which quantization path gets us nearest to target while keeping p95 latency under 500ms.
- Batching policy: recommended batch sizes / policy for interactive (we typically use continuous batching with max latency cap 50ms).
- Storage/eviction for session-prefix cache: how many KB per simultaneous session do we need to assume, and ops cost.

I'll attach the client CSV template to the HubSpot record and ask for the telemetry tonight. Can you turn around a quick XLS with the three scenarios (25/40/60%) and a short note on risk (quality regressions, latency tradeoffs)?

Thanks — appreciate a fast run on this.
Aditya
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Clark <sara.clark@integronhealth.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@integronhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — session cache sizing & rough $/1M targets

Hi Sara / Tom — thanks for the quick reply and the budget transparency. Attached is the costing workbook with the three hit-rate scenarios you requested plus notes on the runtime configuration that underpins each row. Highlights below: 

What we modeled (attached: costing_scenarios_25-40-60_hit.xlsx):
- Conservative baseline (25% hit): effective cost ~ $62 / 1M tokens (assumes int8 quantization, conservative batching due to interactive tail, and 75% reduction in token work on cache hits).
- Mid scenario (40% hit): effective cost ~ $48 / 1M tokens (same runtime, better prefix coverage).
- Aggressive optimization (60% hit + aggressive batching / int4 path): effective cost ~ $35 / 1M tokens but this requires prompt standardization and an A/B run to monitor quality drift.

Recommendations / next steps:
1) Pilot configuration: run the pilot on the int8 path with prefix cache enabled and a 48-hour telemetry feed. That gets us close to your $45 / 1M target if we can push hit toward 40% during the pilot.
2) Short workstream: we propose a 1-week prompt-standardization sprint (we'll provide specs) to increase prefix coverage — aim to move from 25% → 40% hit inside pilot window.
3) Deliverables from us: costing workbook + small mutual action plan (attached). From you: 72-hour telemetry export and a named infra reviewer.

I've attached the MA plan and the costing workbook. Let me know if you want a short follow-up call Monday to walk the spreadsheet with Stephanie (she can answer the runtime tradeoffs).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: costing_scenarios_25-40-60_hit.xlsx, Integron_MA_plan_draft.pdf, session_telemetry_template.csv
